Batumi Botanical Garden

Over a hundred hectares on a cape above the sea, with nine floristic zones of the world laid out side by side.

Time needed
3 h
From Tbilisi
380 km · 5:45
Road
Paved
Car needed
Economy class
Season
All year
Entry
~15 ₾

The Batumi Botanical Garden lies north of the city on Green Cape, dropping down a hillside directly above the sea. It was founded in 1912 by the Russian botanist and geographer Andrey Krasnov and now covers more than a hundred hectares, making it one of the largest botanical collections in the region.

Its structure is unusual. The garden is divided into floristic sections, each representing a specific part of the world: East Asia, North America, Australia, the Mediterranean, the Himalayas, Mexico and Colchis are all connected by paths. Thanks to the humid subtropical climate, plants grow here that would not survive anywhere else in Georgia — bamboo groves, eucalyptus, palms and magnolias.

In practical terms:

  • The site is large and steep — the full circuit takes two to three hours
  • The main view opens from the upper paths across the sea and the Green Cape shoreline
  • A shuttle runs between the upper and lower entrances

Spring is the best season, when the magnolias and azaleas flower, but the garden is open all year and stays green through winter. Even on a grey day the light under the canopy suits photography, which is useful given how often the Adjaran coast is overcast.

Practical advice

Wear comfortable shoes: the garden is on a slope with constant climbs and descents, and you will typically cover more than five kilometres. If you would rather not walk it all, enter at the upper gate, exit at the lower one and take the shuttle back. Water and a hat matter in summer, a rain shell in any season — Adjaran weather turns quickly and the paths get slippery. Cafes and toilets are at both entrances. Parking is outside the grounds and charged separately.

How to get there from Tbilisi

It is roughly 380 km and about five and three quarter hours from Tbilisi. Take the E60 down to Batumi, then continue north along the coast road toward Green Cape: from the city centre to the garden is only 9 km, about twenty minutes. The road is paved all the way, though the last section is narrow and winding with limited overtaking. An economy car is entirely sufficient. Fill up in Batumi. On summer days the car park fills up, so arriving early is worthwhile.

Town

Nature
